sources.entry: BotWave - FM broadcasting system with server-client architecture for managing multiple Raspberry Pi transmitters remotely. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Python

summary.one_liner: BotWave is a Python FM broadcasting system that lets Raspberry Pi devices transmit audio over FM radio, either standalone or managed from a central server across multiple Pis.
summary.what_it_does: BotWave broadcasts audio files or live audio output over FM using Raspberry Pi hardware. A single Pi can run the standalone local client (bw-local) with a CLI for uploading, downloading, starting and stopping broadcasts. For multiple Pis, a server (bw-server) connects to clients (bw-client) over the network, with passkey authentication and protocol versioning. The server CLI can target clients by ID, hostname, comma-separated list, or all. Audio files in common formats such as MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC and OGG are converted automatically. The README also describes a queue system, task automation on events and boot, and remote management over WebSocket via the BWSC tool.
use_cases: broadcast audio over FM radio from a Raspberry Pi
manage a network of Raspberry Pi FM transmitters
live stream audio from an application over FM
play playlists of audio files on FM
learning and experimenting with FM broadcasting
remotely control FM broadcasts from a server
how_to_run: curl -sSL -o bw_install.sh <URL from README> && cat bw_install.sh
notable: Standalone local client for a single Pi, or server-client mode for multiple Pis
Live broadcasting of output from any application via ALSA loopback
Remote management over WebSocket with optional passkey, using the BWSC tool
Target clients by ID, hostname, list, or 'all' from the server CLI
Custom handlers (l_ for local, s_ for server) and event-based task automation
caveats: Client requires Raspberry Pi models 2, 3, 4, or Zero; Pi 5 and Pico are not supported, and root access is needed
Broadcasting FM signals may be regulated; the README warns users to check local laws and use a band-pass filter
Requires a wire or antenna on GPIO 4 (pin 7) to broadcast
